implementation_statement: Access control policy POL-02 (2024) was revised and approved 2026-09-15, effective 2026-10-01 (P06). It now covers OT accounts, vendor remote access, and crew tablets. The OT security standard (STD-04) and authenticator standard (STD-06) that carry the procedures are in draft.

provider_if_inherited: Identity provider vendor (SOC 2 Type 2); FMIS vendor (SOC 2 Type 2)
implementation_statement: Office and management accounts are provisioned in the identity provider from the HR system and federated to SYS-01 web, the cloud accounts, SYS-10, and the SYS-12 staff console. Terminations disable identity provider access automatically. Gaps: crew lead tablets at Farms 1 and 2 use 6 shared SYS-01 logins; access reviews are annual (last February 2026); SYS-01 local mobile accounts, SCADA and HMI accounts, and grower portal staff roles are outside the HR feed, and 9 of 25 sampled seasonal leavers kept a SYS-01 mobile account for more than 30 days (P07).
evidence: HR feed configuration; IdP export; SYS-01 user list; access review February 2026

implementation_statement: Account creation, disablement, and removal for identity provider accounts are automated from the HR system.
Identity provider accounts inactive for 45 days are disabled automatically. SYS-01 mobile accounts, SCADA local accounts, and grower portal accounts have no inactivity rule.

provider_if_inherited: FMIS vendor (SOC 2 Type 2); Cloud provider (SOC 2 Type 2)
implementation_statement: Role-based access is enforced in SYS-01 (manager, agronomist, irrigation operator, crew, food safety), the cloud accounts (permission sets from directory groups), SYS-12 (grower, agronomist, settlement analyst, administrator), and SCADA (operator, engineer, administrator). The personnel file share is readable by 48 office accounts, more than need it.
evidence: Role catalogs; file share permissions export 2026-07-15

implementation_statement: IT/OT firewalls at headquarters and the packinghouse (2025) enforce flows between office, SCADA, and packinghouse control networks. Farm 1 and Farm 2 pump-station and fertigation networks are flat with the farm office networks (gap 2). A broad rule at the packinghouse allows the office VLAN to reach the refrigeration and ripening controllers (P07; R-050).

Settlement analysts cannot approve their own settlement runs in SYS-12, and ACH release in the bank portal needs a second approver in finance. Developers at the contract firm can deploy to production without a company approver (gap 6).
evidence: SYS-12 role design; bank dual-control settings; deployment pipeline review

implementation_statement: Cloud administrators use just-in-time elevation through the privileged access broker. Outside the cloud, privileges are standing: 6 directory administrators, 4 SYS-01 administrators, and all 4 SCADA engineer accounts have permanent rights, and the SCADA integrator's shared account has local administrator rights on both SCADA servers (P07).
evidence: Privileged account list (38 accounts); PAM logs

implementation_statement: Security functions (EDR console, firewall management, backup vault) are limited to named IT and security staff. SCADA security settings can be changed by any engineer account.
IT administrators have separate administrator accounts for cloud and directory work. SCADA engineers use the same account for daily operation and administration.
Cloud privileged roles are restricted to 5 named staff through the access broker. Directory, SYS-01, ERP, and SCADA privileged accounts are not brokered (PAM extension planned 2027-03-31).
The identity provider locks accounts after 10 failed attempts and applies risk-based sign-in controls. SCADA HMIs lock after 5 failed attempts.

Laptops and desktops lock after 10 minutes. HMIs in the Irrigation Operations Center and packinghouse line PCs stay unlocked by design so operators can respond to alarms; compensating control is a staffed room during operating hours.

provider_if_inherited: Identity provider vendor (SOC 2 Type 2); FMIS vendor (SOC 2 Type 2)
implementation_statement: Web sessions to SYS-01, SYS-10, and SYS-12 end after 12 hours or on identity provider sign-out.

Staff remote access uses the client VPN with MFA. Vendor remote access is not controlled: the SCADA integrator connects through a remote access tool on a SCADA server with one shared account and no MFA, the pivot manufacturer has standing cloud access to all 46 pivots, and the refrigeration contractor connects a laptop on site (gap 1).
evidence: VPN configuration; remote tool inventory; P07 test

implementation_statement: Vendor sessions will be brokered, approved per session, and recorded through the privileged access broker by 2026-12-31 (POAM-003).
Office Wi-Fi uses enterprise authentication. Packinghouse scanner Wi-Fi and H-2A housing Wi-Fi are separate networks. A Farm 1 office Wi-Fi network shares the pump-station network (gap 2).
Company tablets and phones are enrolled in mobile device management with a PIN and remote wipe. Crew tablets run SYS-01 in a kiosk profile, but the profile uses shared app logins.
POL-05 forbids company data on personal devices except email and chat through managed apps. Contract developers use their own laptops to reach the Grower Services account (gap 6).

Annual awareness training and quarterly phishing simulations in English and Spanish for office users; June 2026 click rate 9.1%. Crew leads and Irrigation Technicians receive no security content in their pre-season meetings.
Insider threat awareness (reporting unusual setpoint or settlement changes) will be added to the 2026-27 training (POAM-004).
IT administrators receive vendor training. SCADA engineers, Irrigation Technicians, and settlement analysts have no role-based security training (SP 800-82r3 3.3.5).

Logged event types are defined for IT systems (identity, cloud, firewall, EDR, SYS-03, SYS-12). No events are defined or collected for SCADA, PLCs, HMIs, the pivot cloud, or packinghouse controls (gap 2). SYS-01 audit logs exist at the vendor but are not exported.
evidence: SIEM source list; logging standard draft

implementation_statement: Collected IT logs contain user, time, source, event, and outcome fields.

control_name: Audit Record Review, Analysis, and Reporting
implementation_statement: The MSSP reviews IT alerts 24x7. No one reviews SYS-01 audit logs, SCADA alarm and change logs, or settlement change logs (P07).
Cloud and SIEM logs are written to a write-once log bucket in the shared services account with separate access.
IT logs are kept 1 year in the SIEM and 3 years in the locked archive. SCADA historian event logs are kept 90 days on the SCADA server only.
Audit generation is enabled for cloud control planes, identity, firewalls, and endpoints. SCADA audit logging is available but not enabled.
Controls are assessed each year by the co-sourced internal audit firm (P07, 2026-08-03 to 2026-08-21).

Interconnections with the FMIS vendor, ERP and EDI providers, and the payroll provider are covered by contracts. The pivot manufacturer cloud, the equipment dealer portal, 18 contract growers' sensor gateways, and the refrigeration contractor have no written interconnection or security terms (P07).
A POA&M is kept and reported to the audit committee quarterly (P07 poam.csv, 24 items).
Internal authorization decision recorded in SSP section 4.2 (accepted with conditions, 2026-09-15).
Monthly metrics for IT (patching, scans, EDR health, phishing) go to the CFO and the vCISO. OT and Grower Services metrics are not collected.

implementation_statement: Added by tailoring: annual external penetration test of the grower portal (last 2025-11; 2 medium findings closed 2026-01). Not in the Moderate baseline, added because SYS-12 is internet-facing and in SOC 2 scope.
Configuration management is addressed in POL-01 and POL-02. The configuration standard (STD-01) and OT security standard (STD-04) are in draft (gap 8).
Cloud guardrails and endpoint baselines exist for IT. There are no documented baselines for SCADA servers, HMIs, PLC configurations, or the grower portal build (P07).

responsible_role: Director of Irrigation and Water Resources
implementation_statement: IT changes go through a weekly change meeting. PLC logic, HMI screens, fertigation recipes, ripening room programs, and settlement calculation changes have no change records or second reviewer (gap 6; P07).
regulatory_driver: CSF 2.0 ID.RA-07 (benchmark); SP 800-82r3 6.2.4; N11-R01 (21 CFR 121.135 used as a voluntary checklist)

responsible_role: Director of Irrigation and Water Resources
implementation_statement: Impact analysis is done informally for IT changes. OT and settlement changes are not analyzed for safety or processing-integrity impact before deployment.
Production changes in the cloud need elevated roles. SCADA and PLC programs can be changed by any engineer account or the integrator's shared account.
Cloud organization guardrails block public storage and unencrypted volumes. Benchmark scans of 10 servers found 31% of settings deviating (P07). SCADA servers run the integrator's default build.
Unneeded services are disabled on cloud workloads. SCADA servers run a remote access tool, a web browser, and email (P07).

IT asset inventory is complete for endpoints and cloud. The OT and IoT inventory covers about 1,600 of about 2,900 devices (55%), and the field sensor and valve controller counts come from installer invoices (gap 2).
Endpoint inventory updates automatically through EDR and MDM. OT devices added by installers are not reported to IT.
Users cannot install software on managed laptops and desktops; requests go through the service desk.
Contingency planning is covered by POL-03 and the contingency and recovery standard STD-07 (draft, due 2026-12-31).

An IT disaster recovery plan (2024) covers SYS-02, SYS-03, and the cloud workloads. It does not cover SCADA, PLC recovery, packinghouse controls, freeze protection, or Grower Services, and it predates this BIA (P07).
The IT plan is not yet coordinated with the packinghouse downtime procedures, the food safety recall plan, or the incident runbooks (P08).
IT staff walk through the DR plan yearly. Crew leads, packinghouse supervisors, and Irrigation Technicians are not trained on cyber downtime procedures.
Restore tests cover file services quarterly. SCADA servers, PLC programs, the farm data hub, and the grower portal have never been restore-tested (gap 3).
Cloud backups are stored in the backup account in a second region.

Cloud workloads can be restored in a second region. The Irrigation Operations Center has no alternate site; SCADA can run from the second server in the packinghouse control room only if the network path is up.
Headquarters and the packinghouse have dual internet circuits. Farm 2 has a single circuit, and the Farm 1 and Farm 2 pump stations depend on one licensed radio link each (R-042).

Daily write-once backups of the operations and Grower Services accounts to the backup account (35 days, separate credentials). SCADA servers are backed up weekly to a network storage device on the same network, and 31 of 68 PLC and HMI programs have no company-held copy (gap 3).
evidence: Backup reports (30 of 30 days, July 2026); PLC program list

implementation_statement: Backup integrity is checked by the backup service for cloud workloads. SCADA backups are never verified.
Cloud workloads can be rebuilt from templates. SCADA rebuild depends on the integrator's media and a support call; no recovery procedure is written.

Office users, administrators, and grower portal staff have unique identities. Crew lead tablets use 6 shared SYS-01 logins, the SCADA integrator uses one shared account, and 2 HMIs use a shared operator login (gap 4).
evidence: IdP export; SYS-01 and SCADA user lists

implementation_statement: MFA is enforced for all privileged identity provider and cloud accounts. SCADA engineer accounts and the integrator account have no MFA.
Push MFA with number matching for all office users. Grower portal users have optional MFA (31% enrolled).
Device certificates for pivot modems and LoRaWAN gateways are planned with the OT segmentation project (2027-03-31).
Identifiers are assigned from the HR record and never reused.

Identity provider passwords follow a 14-character minimum with a banned list. Default credentials were found on 3 ripening room controllers and the cold storage refrigeration controller (P07; R-050), and 2 of 10 sampled pivot modems use the manufacturer default.

provider_if_inherited: Grower portal hosted in company cloud account
implementation_statement: About 140 grower portal users have unique accounts with email verification. MFA is optional.
POL-03 Incident Response Policy revised 2026-09-15; runbooks in P08.
IT and security staff are trained yearly. Farm Managers, the Packinghouse Manager, and the Director of Food Safety have not been trained on their incident roles.
Tabletop exercises for both P08 runbooks scheduled for 2026-11-10 (ransomware) and 2027-01-20 (OT integrity).
The MSSP contains IT endpoint threats and escalates within 30 minutes. OT containment steps, food safety hold decisions, and grower communications were not defined before P08.
evidence: Incident log (22 incidents in 12 months); P08

implementation_statement: Incidents are tracked in the service desk security queue with severity and timestamps.
Staff report suspected incidents to the service desk security line; the P08 matrix lists external notices and clocks.
The MSSP and the insurer's panel forensics firm provide incident response assistance.
An IT incident response plan exists (2024). The two P08 runbooks (approved 2026-09-15) add OT, food safety, crisis management, and legal steps; neither has been exercised.

responsible_role: Director of Irrigation and Water Resources
implementation_statement: Pump, VFD, and PLC maintenance is scheduled in SYS-01 work orders. Maintenance by the integrator and refrigeration contractor is not recorded.

responsible_role: Director of Irrigation and Water Resources
implementation_statement: Nonlocal maintenance by the SCADA integrator and the pivot manufacturer is standing, not approved per session, and not recorded (gap 1).
IT media are wiped or destroyed with certificates. Replaced HMIs and line PCs are returned to vendors without wiping records.
Badge access lists for headquarters, the IOC, and the packinghouse control room are approved by managers and reviewed yearly.

responsible_role: Director of Irrigation and Water Resources
implementation_statement: Headquarters, the IOC, and the packinghouse control room use badge readers. The 54 well pump stations and 14 fertigation skids use padlocks on a common key, and 8 of 12 sampled stations had unlocked control panels (P07).
Cameras cover headquarters and the packinghouse. Pump stations are not monitored.
The IOC server room has cooling and temperature alarms; SCADA servers are on a UPS and generator.
This SSP is the first for the FMICP (approved 2026-09-15). It is reviewed yearly and after major changes.
Acceptable use policy POL-05 is acknowledged at hire and yearly (English and Spanish).
A target OT architecture (zones and conduits per SP 800-82r3 section 5) exists in draft. Farms 1 and 2 are not yet built to it.

Background checks for office, IT, and settlement staff; H-2A workers are screened through the program process.
Terminations disable identity provider access the same day. SYS-01 mobile accounts, SCADA accounts, badges, and pump-station keys are removed manually and late (P07: 9 of 25 sampled leavers).
Transfers between farms do not trigger review of SYS-01 farm permissions.
Contracts with the MSSP and FMIS vendor include security terms. The SCADA integrator, pivot vendor, refrigeration contractor, and development firm contracts do not.
The FMICP is categorized Moderate (SSP section 6).
Annual risk assessment per SP 800-30 completed 2026-07-31 (P01, 50 risks).
Supply chain risks are in P01 (R-014, R-027, R-045) but are not assessed per vendor.
Authenticated scans of IT systems run quarterly (moving to monthly). OT is not scanned; no passive OT discovery exists (P07).
Critical components are identified in the BIA (P05). Freeze protection and cold chain are rated most critical.
Security requirements are in new IT purchases. OT and agricultural equipment purchases (pivots, sensors, graders) have no security requirements.
The grower portal uses the cloud provider's managed services and a web application firewall. No documented security design principles were given to the development firm.

SOC 2 reports for the FMIS vendor, MSSP, identity provider, and cloud provider are on file. Reviews happen only at onboarding; 38 vendors with data or system access have never been reassessed (gap 5).
The development firm runs unit tests and an annual penetration test is commissioned. No static analysis, dependency scanning, or settlement calculation regression tests exist (gap 6).
A secure development standard (STD-11) for the development firm is due 2027-03-31 (POAM-017).

responsible_role: Director of Irrigation and Water Resources
implementation_statement: 2 HMIs run an operating system past end of support; the integrator supports them only on that version. Compensating controls: no internet, no email, removable media blocked.
Cloud network hub and firewall control traffic between accounts and sites. IT/OT boundaries exist at headquarters and the packinghouse; Farms 1 and 2 have no OT boundary (gap 2).

control_name: Deny by Default, Allow by Exception
implementation_statement: Cloud and headquarters OT firewalls deny by default. The packinghouse firewall has an any-to-any rule between the office VLAN and the controller VLAN (P07).
TLS 1.2 or higher for all web and API traffic; IPsec between sites. Pump-station radio links and LoRaWAN traffic use vendor encryption that has not been reviewed.
Company-managed keys in the cloud key service; separate keys for the backup account.
Provider-validated cryptographic modules for storage and transport encryption.
Cloud storage, SaaS, and laptops are encrypted. SCADA servers, the local backup storage device, and packinghouse line PCs are not.
IT patches monthly (critical within 30 days, 82% on time in Q2 2026). SCADA servers and HMIs were last patched in 2025-03; PLC firmware is never updated.
EDR blocks malware on laptops and desktops. Packinghouse line PCs run EDR in detect-only mode; SCADA servers run the integrator-approved antivirus with signatures 4 months old.
The MSSP monitors IT systems 24x7. There is no OT network monitoring and no alerting on setpoint, schedule, or recipe changes (gap 2).
The security team receives CISA advisories, including ICS advisories, and FMIS vendor bulletins.

responsible_role: Director of Irrigation and Water Resources
implementation_statement: Integrity tailoring: SYS-01 keeps an edit history for records. There is no integrity check on PLC programs, fertigation recipes, ripening programs, or settlement calculation code.
The settlement service validates grower IDs and price ranges. Grade data from the optical graders is not reconciled to packed cases before settlement.

responsible_role: Director of Food Safety and Quality
implementation_statement: Retention rules exist for finance records. No retention or disposal rule covers Produce Safety, pesticide, H-2A, traceability, biometric, or personnel records in company systems (gap 10, gap 11).
A supply chain risk management plan will be part of STD-03 (2026-12-31).
Purchasing requires security review for new SaaS. OT and equipment suppliers are not reviewed.
Supplier assessment is done at onboarding only; 4 Tier 1 SOC 2 reviews completed in 2026 (P09).
